$comment: Posterize type direction. Fonts come from foundations/typography/source/pairings.json (rated in fit) or from newPairings below (Google Fonts only, credits checked against Google Fonts listings; see research.md 7). Sizes are rules of thumb unless a source is given.
character: Bold, condensed grotesques and gothics, the type of wood-type bills, protest posters and gig posters: heavy enough to stand next to a solid ink plate, narrow enough to be big. Set tight, in sentence case, on flat colour. The image is loud, so the type is plain and strong, not decorated.

anatomy.$comment: What to look for when judging a typeface for this approach.

weight.why: The headline must hold its own beside a solid ink plate that covers 20-35% of the subject.

width.why: Condensed faces allow big sizes in a narrow text block, as on posters.

contrast.why: Even strokes print and screen cleanly, like the plates; thin hairlines break up at small sizes and in halftone.

terminals.why: Echo the hard, cut edges of the plates.

counters.why: Black condensed faces close up when reversed out of colour; check the e and a at the smallest headline size.

xHeight.why: Readable at distance and at thumbnail size.

avoid: Light and thin weights for headlines
Calligraphic or high-contrast serifs for headlines

fit.$comment: core = recommended, good = works, accent = special cases, avoid = not for this approach.

bricolage-figtree.why: Bricolage Grotesque at 800 with its narrow width axis is a punchy poster grotesque; Figtree stays plain for body.

schibsted.why: One strict grotesk with heavy weights; hierarchy by size alone suits the flat, graphic plates.

plex.why: IBM Plex Sans Bold is sturdy and even; the engineered feel fits technical or civic posters.

instrument.why: The condensed serif suits culture and editorial duotones, but a single regular weight is light beside a solid ink plate.

source.why: Use the Source Sans 3 Black for headlines in text-heavy pieces; the serif display is too bookish for posters.

young-onest.why: Young Serif's chunky forms can work for food and hospitality posters; keep the image at 2-3 levels so the two do not compete.

fraunces-commissioner.why: Fraunces Black recalls 1970s display print; only for a deliberate retro piece.

nunito.why: Rounded terminals and soft forms fight the hard-cut plates and read childish next to them.

alegreya.why: Calligraphic, literary forms contradict the mechanical print look.

newPairings.name: Protest Poster
newPairings.mood: Loud, urgent and plain. A tall, condensed advertising gothic for big headlines over a sturdy grotesque with width and weight axes.
newPairings.bestFor: Posters, gig and event posters, social posts, campaigns that need to shout clearly.

display.case: Sentence case; capitals only for labels of one to three words
display.notes: A reworking of a traditional advertising sans serif, reshaped for screens. One weight only: hierarchy comes from size. The related family Antonio, built from Anton, adds weights.

body.style: Grotesque with width and weight axes
body.designer: Héctor Gatti and the Omnibus-Type team
body.notes: Omnibus-Type is a collective foundry in Buenos Aires. Archivo Narrow and Archivo Black are sister families; the condensed widths (wdth 62-75) can also set subheads.

newPairings.name: Civic Gothic
newPairings.mood: Public and confident. A condensed American gothic built for a city's signs and posters, over a slightly rounded grotesque drawn from California road signs.
newPairings.bestFor: Civic, transport, sport and community campaigns; events; outdoor and wayfinding-like pieces.

display.case: Sentence case; capitals only for labels
display.notes: Made for the City of Chicago's design system; its tall forms draw on Chicago's railway, political and dance history. Sister families Big Shoulders Stencil and Inline exist; Google Fonts also serves a combined 'Big Shoulders' family.

body.style: Low-contrast grotesque with slightly rounded forms
body.notes: Static family in three widths (Barlow, Semi Condensed, Condensed), 9 weights each; based on California's plates, highway signs, buses and trains.

handwritten.$comment: Handwritten accent faces from foundations/typography/source/handwritten.json. use: none | accent (one short element) | core (part of the style). A product picks one in brand.json -> typography.hand.
handwritten.why: Flat posterized photos need solid, heavy type to hold against them; thin, irregular hand strokes break up on the colour bands.

typeWithArt.weightMatch: Headline stems should be at least as thick as the thinnest ink shapes in the image (about 3 units on a 400 artboard) and visually as dark as the ink plate: use 700-900, or Anton.
typeWithArt.scaleMatch: Headline cap height 1/4 to 1/2 of the subject's face height, so the image stays the focal point and the words are still the second thing seen.
typeWithArt.placement: Text on flat ground or a flat plate only, aligned to the image block's edge or to the grid's first column; never across the image.
typeWithArt.colour: Headline in ink or the combination's text role; never in the accent if the accent is a middle tone of the image (it would read as part of the picture).

sizes.$comment: Headline cap height as a share of the canvas height, and body text minimums. Rules of thumb; larger than humanist-minimal because condensed faces are narrow.
sizes.viewingDistance: Sign-industry rule of thumb: about 1 inch (25 mm) of letter height for every 10 feet (3 m) of viewing distance for basic legibility; double it for comfortable reading.

measure.source: Bringhurst, The Elements of Typographic Style

setting.headlineCharsNote: Characters per headline line with condensed faces; break by sense, not by fit.
setting.case: Sentence case everywhere. Capitals only for labels of one to three words.
setting.rag: Ragged right, left-aligned. No justified text.
setting.numbers: Dates, times and prices in the display face when they are the message, otherwise in the mono with tabular figures.

rules: Three sizes and two weights per piece.
Type on flat colour only, never across the image.
No handwriting, grunge or outline fonts.
